primitives.name: Customer Lifetime Value
primitives.verbatim_quote: Track your over time — beating the closing line is the clearest public proof of an edge.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'CLV': 'USD Customer Lifetime Value', 'R_t': 'Revenue generated from customer t (USD)', 'C_t': 'Cost of service at time t (USD)', 'P_t': 'Probability of customer retention at time t (dimensionless)', 'r': 'Discount rate (annualized, dimensionless)', 'I_0': 'Initial acquisition cost (USD)'}
primitives.assumptions: (1) Exponential decay of retention probability; (2) Constant marginal revenue; (3) Stable discount factor.
primitives.breakdown_regime: CLV becomes negative when churn rate exceeds the break-even threshold, signaling unsustainable business models.

layer2.mapping: Maps to a discounted cash flow (DCF) model with survival analysis, where retention replaces perpetuity growth.
layer2.telemetry: Sudden drops in CLV imply external shocks or internal friction points.
